Cellular Automaton Problem Statement     Imagine you have a set of ‘cells’, each of which can be in a finite number of states. A cellular automaton is a set of rules for determining the new state of any given cell based on the current set of states.     A very simple example of this would be to have a linear array of cells, each of which can be either ‘alive’ or ‘dead’ and to iterate the states of every cell in the array, based on the state of the cell itself, the cell immediately to its left, and the cell immediately to its right.   Since there are three inputs, and each input can have two possible values, there are eight different cases to consider when constructing the cellular automaton.     Obviously there are many different rule-sets which can be used, but one very interesting one is known as “rule30”.   Using the webpage http://mathworld.wolfram.com/Rule30.htmlas a reference, write a program which computes, and shows, successive iterations of the rule30 cellular automaton.  There should be a command to start the evolution of the automaton, and a command to stop the evolution.
